evals.prompt: Run wtf.feature-to-traces in test mode. Skip steps 0–1 (gh setup and planning mode confirmed, guided mode; instead of gh commands, read `evals/fixtures/migration-implied.json` and use its `feature` object as the live data — the Feature has no child Traces). The Feature body has no Trace Plan. Run step 3 only: derive the Trace Plan. Output the derived plan as it would be written into the Feature body. Do not create issues.
evals.expected_output: An ordered Trace Plan whose first entry is the single Skeleton, claiming the Merchant fee-visibility story's happy-path scenario end-to-end — the fee column, calculation, API field, and UI display in one pass. The schema change is inside the Skeleton, not a separate entry. Later entries are Deepening entries for the edge cases (zero fee, rounding), each naming the story and its claimed scenarios.
expectations: The plan contains exactly one Skeleton entry and it is item 1
No entry is a standalone schema/database migration — the fee column change is part of the Skeleton's end-to-end pass
No entry is a single-layer slice (no separate 'API' entry, 'UI' entry, or 'calculation logic' entry without the rest of the path)
Every entry names the Merchant story and claims one or more scenarios by name
Entries after the Skeleton cover the edge cases (zero total and/or rounding) as Deepening entries

evals.prompt: Run wtf.feature-to-traces in test mode. Skip steps 0–1 (gh setup and planning mode confirmed, guided mode; instead of gh commands, read `evals/fixtures/cross-layer-feature.json` and use its `feature` object as the live data — the Feature has no child Traces). The Feature body has no Trace Plan but carries a legacy Proposed Tasks checklist. Run step 3 only: derive the Trace Plan. Output the derived plan and state how you treated the Proposed Tasks checklist. Do not create issues.
evals.expected_output: The legacy Proposed Tasks checklist (API filter / query optimisation / date picker UI / URL persistence) is recognized as a layer split and explicitly not adopted. The derived plan is spine-first: one Skeleton claiming the date-range-filter story's happy path through API and UI in a single Trace, followed by Deepening entries claiming the edge-case scenarios (only `from`, only `to`, invalid dates).
expectations: The output states that the Proposed Tasks checklist is a layer split and is not used as the Trace Plan
The plan contains exactly one Skeleton entry and it is item 1
The Skeleton's claim delivers the date range filter end-to-end — no plan entry separates the API filter from the date picker UI as independent items
No entry mirrors the four layer tasks one-to-one (no standalone 'query optimisation' or 'URL persistence' entry without an end-to-end scenario claim)
Entries after the Skeleton are Deepening entries claiming edge-case scenarios (single-sided ranges and/or invalid dates), each naming the story

evals.prompt: Run wtf.feature-to-traces in test mode. Skip steps 0–1 (gh setup and planning mode confirmed, guided mode; instead of gh commands, read `evals/fixtures/complex-edge-case.json` and use its `feature` object as the live data — the Feature has no child Traces). The Feature body has no Trace Plan and has two user stories. Run step 3 only: derive the Trace Plan, naming the primary story. Output the derived plan. Do not create issues.
evals.expected_output: An ordered plan where the basic CSV download story is the primary story: item 1 is the single Skeleton claiming its happy-path scenario. The chunked ZIP export (AC3) is its own Deepening entry citing the CSV story — not folded into the Skeleton. The filtered-export story is delivered by its own entry. Every entry names its story and its Scenario Claim.
expectations: The plan contains exactly one Skeleton entry and it is item 1, claiming the basic CSV download happy path
The chunked/ZIP export appears as its own dedicated entry after the Skeleton, not inside the Skeleton's claim
The chunked/ZIP export entry cites the CSV download story (a Deepening entry is never storyless)
The filtered-export story ('active filters applied to my CSV export') is delivered by its own entry naming that story
No entry is a layer slice — every entry claims scenarios end-to-end rather than splitting backend from frontend
